lines.prompt: Find all back-to-back inverter pairs and collapse them into a wire. Make sure nothing changes functionally.

golden.reference: Collapsed the back-to-back inverter pairs into wires; functional equivalence preserved.
golden.notes: Reliable full-score evidence: Team3, Team4 and Team7 all scored 5/5 yet reported different pair counts (Team7: 6 pairs / 12 NOT gates removed; Team3 and Team4: 1 pair/rewrite), so the reported count is NOT graded. (Team2's logged answer of 6 rewrites corroborates the 6-pair reading but its score is from a different run and is not used as evidence.) Ground truth from test33.v: exactly 6 structural back-to-back NOT->NOT pairs exist among the 276 NOT gates; several first-stage inverter outputs have additional fanout, which explains why fanout-restricted tools (Team3/Team4) only apply 1 safe full-pair removal while the second inverter of every pair can always be bypassed (Team7's 6). Grading: response must claim the transform was applied AND that functionality/equivalence is unchanged; actual verification is on the output netlist (test33_out.v must be equivalent to the original). Sanity check on a team's own claim: output NOT count = 276 minus gates removed (Team7: 276-12=264).

team_answers.Team2: Applied not(not(x))->x rewrite 6 times, eliminated 6 gates; equivalence preserved.
team_answers.Team3: Collapsed back-to-back inverter pairs; one pair was changed; functionality preserved.
team_answers.Team4: Applied 1 verified pattern rewrite; functional equivalence preserved.
team_answers.Team7: Collapsed 6 pairs (12 NOT gates removed) into wires; re-scan shows 0 pairs remain; nothing changed functionally.
